text: Be clever and fun, but don't be mean. Rule two: see rule one. Clueso looked for a rule three, found a laundry basket, and gave up.
A team can only prank another team once. Make it count. Spend it on something better than a bag of balloons. Clueso is naming no names, just a color. Orange.
Try to prank someone who hasn't been pranked yet. Sharing the fun is encouraged. Hogging it is how a For Sale sign ends up in a case file.
No photo, no points. Proof goes to the game group. A PNN case file is a bonus, not a receipt, and Clueso's filing cabinet is already full of laundry.
Pranks and photos must be posted by October 22 to earn points. 'I meant to post it' is not a deadline. It is a Black Webb Bandits origin story.
Nothing may be damaged or destroyed. Borrowing is a grey area. Grey areas are for socks and for cover stories about how long you've had the dog.
Never target or frighten a child. Spooky is a vibe. Scared is a problem. Even the Silver Bullets, who are 'slow, unsure, and completely disoriented,' know this.
Do not prank to wake anyone up. Sleep schedules are not a game mechanic. If your plan needs an alarm clock, it is a bad plan with a worse alarm.
Never sign up or share anyone's information with outsiders who aren't playing. Your neighbor's email address is not a treat. Keep it classified, like the Area 51 Bureau's recycling used to be.

Blur house numbers, license plates, phone numbers, and anyone who didn't sign up before you post. PNN blurred a plate, a phone number, and a person out of PNN-005 so you don't have to. You're welcome, Posse.
Wait for the witches' instructions before bribing. Early bribes get a NO and must be repeated. The Black Webb Bandits have the data on this. The data is humbling.
A surprise only works if the victim is surprised. Post your proof after they have seen the prank, not before. The Pyro Posse is available for questions. Quickly, before they delete them.

Plan around public schedules, not private lives. If you have to guess where someone is, you are doing Purrveillance wrong. If you have to tap a phone, you are doing crime. Clueso is a little jealous either way.
Fire is not part of the game. A paper flame on a stick has 100% of the drama and 0% of the paperwork. The Pyro Posse knows this. Mostly. They have a lot of paper flames.
A good prank is funny to the victim, too. The test: would they say 'good one' at the Halloween party? If the honest answer is 'I'd say something, but not that,' go back to the drawing board.
Count your pranks before you announce them. A certain orange team claimed three. The correct number was four. Clueso won't say which team. He will say it has a lot of paper flames.
Your costume doesn't need to be expensive. It needs to be committed. A half-committed costume is just laundry, and the neighborhood has had enough of that this week.
Roast the team theme, never the families, the neighbors, or the house itself. A team named after underwear has already agreed to the premise.
Bring treats before you ask whether someone is a witch. Manners are the only form of bribery Clueso endorses, and the only kind some teams are still learning to do on time.
Spotted something? Send it to the Tip Line with a photo you have permission to share. Clueso has now read the tip pile three times and found zero tips about the pink team. He finds this suspicious.
Think PNN got it wrong? The Corrections Desk is open. Clueso reads every correction carefully, then ignores the ones that hurt, then files them under 'Unfair.'
Plan your prank like a case file: setup, escalation, payoff. Skipping straight to 'photo' is how a team ends up with a clothesline, a bonfire's worth of confidence, and no plot.
The best pranks leave people laughing and nobody cleaning. If cleanup takes longer than setup, you have built a chore. Somebody out there is still finding mystery white bits in their lawn.
Don't spoil the surprise. Don't forget your own prank. Don't delete the evidence. A certain orange team is working through that list and is, so far, a perfect zero for three.
A tagline on someone else's poster is not a strategy. Make a plan, Silver Bullets. Clueso believes in you, and he doesn't believe in anyone.
The truth is out there. So is your trash can. Clueso recommends bringing it in before the Pyro Posse brings balloons.
Rehearse saying hello. It is the hardest part of any covert operation. Also, nice dog. How long have you had it?
The starting line is a real place, and the starting signal is a real thing. Locate both, then try arriving between them.
The Crimson Crew has yet to appear in a case file. Clueso finds this suspicious and slightly insulting. Do something. Anything. Within the rules, and loudly.

If you see the Prowling Purrpetrators doing anything, tell Clueso. If you see them doing nothing, tell him louder. A team this quiet is either innocent or very good, and Clueso does not believe in innocent.
